title: A stored Failed state for an operation: a record of the failed generation, through the history (#4245 step 2)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
## Summary

This is a step-2 item of the UI plan #4245: "A stored failed state". The maintainer accepted the step-2 items as design issues (comment of 2026-11-27 08:09 on #4245). Code starts only when the maintainer accepts the design note below. The note uses the part stamps of #4479, but it does not need them.

## What happens today

- A generation that fails returns a `CommandError`. The window shows "generate failed: …" as a refusal line, puts a marker where the generator refused (#261 part 2) and draws the moves that it made as a ghost (#261 part 3) (`land_generation`, `crates/ui/src/gen_worker.rs`).
- Nothing goes into the operation. The old cache and the old stamp stay. Thus after the refusal line goes away:
  - the Browser and the operation page show the old state: "Stale · … · 1234 moves cached", or "never generated";
  - a save and a load lose the failure;
  - MCP `generate` names the refusal one time. A later `get_job` does not show it.
- The page shows "Blocked · {why}" only for a tool problem that the tool gate finds before generation (`tool_gate::tool_problem_of`, `op_page.rs`).

The mockups E1 and E2 of #4245 show "failed" as an operation state, with its reason, in the Browser, on the operation page and in the issues pane.

## Design note (for acceptance)

### Rule 1: a failure is a record about the inputs that it saw

A failed generation writes a record on the operation:

```
GenFailure { stamp: GenStamp, message: String, at: Option<[f64; 3]> }
```

`stamp` is the stamp of the inputs that the failed run read (the same `op_stamp` that a successful run stores). The record applies only while the live stamp is equal to `stamp`. When the user changes an input, the record no longer applies, and the operation shows its normal state again (Never or Stale). A generation that succeeds removes the record.

### Rule 2: `OpStatus::Failed`

`status_of` returns a new state, `Failed`, when a record applies. The order:

1. A record applies: `Failed`.
2. No cache: `Never`.
3. The stored stamp is equal to the live stamp: `Ok`.
4. Else: `Stale`.

A new enum value makes the compiler find each `match` on `OpStatus` (about 25 places in `crates/app` and `crates/ui`). Each one gets a decision, not a default arm.

### Rule 3: the post gate refuses a failed operation

The post gate already refuses Stale and Never. It refuses `Failed` too, with the message of the record. This only adds a refusal. No program that posts today and has no failure changes. An old cache stays on screen for reference ("Failed · {why} · 1234 moves from an earlier run"), but it never posts while the record applies.

### Rule 4: the record goes through the history

AGENTS.md "Everything Is a Command": a change of the document goes through a command. A successful generation is an undo step today (`GenerateOperation`). A failure becomes the command `RecordGenerationFailure` with the same shape:

- `apply` writes the record and keeps the old cache;
- `undo` restores the old record (usually none).

One failed generation is one undo step, as one successful generation is.

The worker thread does not change. `land_generation` executes the new command in place of the plain refusal line. The refusal line, the marker and the ghost stay.

### Rule 5: the project file

`OperationDto` gets one optional field, `failure` (stamp, message, location). `PROJECT_VERSION` goes up by one. The step-up is the version alone. A save without a record writes no key, so these files keep their bytes. If #4479 lands in the same cut, the two fields can share one version step.

### Rule 6: MCP

- `generate` keeps its refusal text and stops as today.
- `get_job` and the operation list show `"status": "failed"` and the field `failure` (the message and the location). This is an addition. No tool changes its arguments.

### Rule 7: the words

The state word is "Failed" (one word, with the reason after a dot: "Failed · Pocket 1: the tool does not fit the corner R2.0"). This follows the words that #4245 accepted: "Up to date", "Needs regenerate", "fold".

### What does not change

- No toolpath and no posted G-code changes for an operation without a failure.
- `GenStamp` keeps its bytes.
- The tool gate ("Blocked · {why}") stays. It is a live check before generation.

### Options dropped

- **Keep the failure in the window state only (not saved).** This is simple. But a load loses it, and MCP cannot read it. Dropped.
- **Remove the old cache on a failure.** This makes Never and Failed the same. But the user loses the old moves for reference. Dropped: the post gate refuses the operation in all cases (rule 3).
- **Write the record without the history.** This keeps undo as it is. But it is a direct write to a document field, which AGENTS.md forbids. Dropped.

## Tests (when the note is accepted)

- A generation that the generator refuses gives `Failed` with the message. A save and a load keep it.
- An input edit after the failure gives `Stale` (an old cache) or `Never` (no cache).
- A successful generation removes the record.
- The post refuses a `Failed` operation and names the message.
- Undo after the failure restores the old state. Redo writes the record again.
- MCP `get_job` shows `"status": "failed"` and the message.
- A project without the field saves and loads the same bytes.

## Effort and safety

`effort:high`. It adds a state, a command, a project-file field and a post refusal. The post change only adds a refusal. The review must check rule 3 and that no `match` on `OpStatus` uses a default arm for `Failed`.

Done means: the maintainer accepts the design note; then one PR does rules 1 to 7 with the tests above.

Parent: #4245. Related: #4479 (part stamps), #261 (refusal location and ghost).
